messages:
emma_support: Escalation from ACME: /v1/rerank/batch returns scores that don't line up with per-query candidate lists. Multiple queries in one payload — second and later queries' scores seem shifted by a constant offset. Customer noticed after a spike this morning.

sanjay_ml: Can you paste the exact request body (sanitized) and any response snippet? Quick check: are they using an explicit per_query_counts array or sending flattened candidates?

emma_support: Pasted (redacted):
```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "text": "get user profile"},
    {"id": "q2", "text": "list recent orders"}
  ],
  "candidates": [
    ["u1_profile", "u1_details"],
    ["order_1", "order_2", "order_3"]
  ],
  "top_k": 3
}
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{
  "scores": [0.92, 0.88, 0.11, 0.65, 0.70]
}
```
Customer expects 2+3=5 scores grouped as [2 for q1, 3 for q2] but actual mapping looks like first 2 scores map to q1, then next 3 seem shifted (e.g. q2 gets [0.11,0.65,0.70] where 0.11 should belong to q1 candidate 3 if flattening happened).

sanjay_ml: That mismatch looks like an index alignment bug between the flattening routine and the per-query offsets. Any req_id or server logs? Also which SDK/version are they using?

emma_support: Req-id from customer: rw-req-2026-03-17-ACME-9876. They hit the HTTP 200 with wrong scores (no 4xx). Using python-sdk 1.8.2.

oliver_platform: Noted — we shipped a change in the batch serializer last night (PR #2345) to concat nested lists for performance. It collapsed candidate arrays into a single flattened vector but I thought we adjusted offsets. Will look now.

marta_sre: Any latency/timeouts correlated? We saw an infra autoscale at 08:41 UTC but no errors in infra. This looks logical not infra.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1123 — tagging engineering oncall. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1123

sanjay_ml: Quick repro we can run locally (useful to validate):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-rw-req-id: rw-repro-1718802460' \
  -d '{"queries":[{"text":"a"},{"text":"b"}],"candidates":[["A1","A2"],["B1","B2","B3"]],"top_k":3}'
```
If server flattens incorrectly you should see 5 scores but mis-ordered mapping.

emma_support: Ran the curl with the customer's payload (sanitized) against staging with that req-id. Repro ✅ — scores returned: [0.82,0.79,0.05,0.61,0.58]. Verified by manually mapping: third score (0.05) actually corresponds to A3 non-existent -> clearly misaligned.

oliver_platform: Confirmed locally. Bug introduced in serializer: when nested arrays length >1 we prepend a cumulative offset header but forgot to update offsets from streaming concat. I'm rolling a revert of PR #2345 to staging now.

marta_sre: Coordinate with deploy windows — what's the rollback plan? Will this require migrations?

oliver_platform: No migrations. Rollback steps: revert PR, run unit tests, deploy to staging (30m), run synthetic rerank suite, then prod (2h). I'll post CI links.

sanjay_ml: Also recommend API-side defensive check: if sum(len(candidates[i]) for i in queries) != len(flat_candidates) OR provided per_query counts don't match, return 400 with message: "candidate/list-length-mismatch: candidates do not align with per-query counts". Prevents silent misalignment. I'll draft a small patch.

emma_support: Customer asked for workaround while we fix: send explicit per-query placeholders so we keep nesting intact (i.e., always send candidates as array-of-arrays and set header X-RW-ENFORCE-NESTING: true). I've suggested they upgrade to python-sdk 1.8.3 which includes a manual serializer toggle. Customer confirmed workaround works for them.

oliver_platform: Pushed revert branch and tests. CI pass on unit tests, running rerank integration suite now. If green I'll queue staging deploy.

support-bot: CI: rerank-integration — started (link: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345).

marta_sre: I'll watch deploy and be ready to roll back infra changes. Also will check metrics for any spike in failed requests post-deploy.

emma_support: Customer updated — they can live with workaround for now. Asked for ETA. Told them ~2h for prod fix.

sanjay_ml: After prod rollback we'll add the API-side validation and a unit test to cover nested/flattened permutations. Also add a small fuzz test to ensure offsets never underflow.

oliver_platform: Staging deploy complete, integration suite green. Scheduling prod deploy in 40m to avoid peak.

emma_support: Thanks all — marking this thread as monitored. Will update ACME when prod is live and verified.

oliver_platform: Prod deploy done. Verified with rw-req-1718802460 — scores now align. Putting follow-up PR to add defensive 400.

emma_support: Customer confirmed fixed and happy. Closing escalation.
